questions.h: Indexes start at 0. Which values are at indexes 2 and 5?
questions.e: Indexes start at 0: a[2] is 15 and a[5] is 42, so 57.

questions.h: push_back adds to the end; back() is the last element.
questions.e: push_back adds 1 at the end: 4 elements, and the last one is 1.

questions.h: The champion starts at a[0] and keeps the smaller value.
questions.e: The champion starts at a[0] and is replaced by any smaller value: the minimum is 1.

questions.code:
int a[] = {1, 2, 3};
for (int i = 2; i >= 0; i--) cout << a[i];
questions.h: The loop starts at the last index and goes down to 0.
questions.e: The loop goes from the last index (2) down to 0, so it prints the array backwards.

questions.h: There is no break, so later matches overwrite pos.
questions.e: There is no break, so every match overwrites pos: the last 7 is at index 2.

questions.q: You add 10^5 numbers, each up to 10^9. Which type does the sum need?
questions.h: How big can the sum get?
questions.e: The sum can reach 10^14, far above int's limit of about 2.1 × 10^9.

questions.h: f keeps the largest value; s keeps the largest value below f.
questions.e: f tracks the largest (35) and s the second-largest distinct value (34). The second 35 is skipped because it equals f.

questions.h: What is the last valid index of an array of size n?
questions.e: Valid indexes are 0 to n − 1. i <= n also reads a[n], which is out of bounds.
